{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish and put the full design on the scratch pad in the first minute: a big left-facing outline with a nose on the left and a swooshy tail on the right. The design had a single start, a top line, and a bottom line that branches off at the nose, so one push could run the whole picture. I laid the start domino and traced most of the top line (stroke 1), which is the backbone everything else hangs from. Late on, I carried the bottom line forward from the belly toward the tail, up to the peak of the bump. At the push, about 116 of the table's 119 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I chose a shape that suits dominoes: gentle curves, no sharp corners, and a large outline that fills the table. I inspected the left stretch of the top line and confirmed it was connected from the start with no gaps. Later I inspected the tail and flagged a jammed domino so it could be fixed before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work early so people weren't bumping each other. I took the top line, Maya took the bottom, and the tail end was shared as the lines approached it. I handed off stretches cleanly and stepped off ends when others took over, which kept the table's hands from colliding. I gave regular updates on what was connected and what was next.

Leadership: I set the direction quickly, invited objections to the animal, and assigned stretches by name. I kept the group aware of the clock, and at the two-minute mark I called for hands off and everyone stepping back before the push. That kept the table calm and organised through the last minutes.", "my_share_percent": 40}
